citations.assessment: Exact named pointer. The following three passages form an explicitly bracketed gloss layer.
The checked text gives the three statements directly to R. Yehoshua ben Levi, without the introductory “Rabbi said.” The gloss reports a different chain and questions it.
The vocalized source omits the extra Rabbi; the checked unvocalized transcription has the abbreviation א״ר parenthetically. The original gloss’s expansion and its chronology remain attributed.
The primary wording has Rav Avira call himself maftir kenesiyot. Rashi describes the function as gathering students and seeing them in and out of the study hall.
Rashi’s adjacent gloss explicitly identifies Rabbi the Great as R. Yehudah Ha-Nasi.
Shabbat 113b:13 has R. Shmuel bar Nahmani directly interpret “under its glory.” The gloss reports an additional Rabbi in the transmission chain and says to remove it.
Both digital Ein Yaakov witnesses lack an extra Rabbi. The ordinary digital text names Shmuel bar Nahmani where Glick has Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
